sections.h2: What is Hamblen County like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Hamblen County is small and busy. Its 176 square miles make it the third-smallest Tennessee county by land area, and almost everything revolves around Morristown, the county seat and largest city. The legislature carved the county out of Jefferson, Grainger and Hawkins counties in 1870 and named it for early settler Hezekiah Hamblen. The courthouse in Morristown was finished in 1874.

Cherokee Lake, a TVA reservoir built during World War II, reaches into the county, although only part of its 400 miles of shoreline is here. Panther Creek State Park is also inside the county line. Interstate 81 crosses it, along with US 11E and US 25E. Large industrial parks on the east, west and south sides hold manufacturing plants, and Walters State Community College is in Morristown. Outside the city you will find White Pine, Russellville, Whitesburg, Talbott, Lowland and Witt.

The Census Bureau reports these numbers for Hamblen County:

  • 68,843 residents in July 2025, a rise of 6.7 percent since April 2020
  • 28,945 housing units, 69.8 percent of them owner-occupied
  • $210,900 as the median owner-occupied home value for 2020 to 2024
  • $55,454 median household income and 14.8 percent of people below the poverty line
  • 258 building permits in 2025

A lower owner-occupancy rate than neighboring Greene County, 69.8 percent against 77.1, leaves a larger share of Hamblen County homes in the hands of landlords or other non-owner occupants.

sections.h2: Which Hamblen County offices deal with property tax?
sections.html:
Everything sits in the Hamblen County Courthouse at 511 West Second North Street, Morristown, TN 37814. Keith Ely, the Assessor of Property since his first election in 2004, is at 423-586-1852. His office handles about 32,000 parcels with a combined appraised value above $3 billion, and it prepares the assessment roll for both Hamblen County and the City of Morristown.

The Trustee, Scotty Long, collects the tax and can be reached at 423-586-6290. A satellite office at 2415 N Davy Crockett Parkway also takes payments. The county commission has fourteen members who set the rate, and it meets on the Thursday after the third Monday of each month at 5:30 p.m. The next meeting is Thursday, November 19, 2026. Its June 25, 2026 agenda included Resolution 26-09, which fixes the tax levy for the fiscal year that began July 1, 2026. Ask the Trustee for the exact county rate, and ask whether the City of Morristown adds its own tax to a given address.

sections.h2: How does Hamblen County calculate a tax bill?
sections.html:
Start with the appraised value from the Assessor, apply the state ratio, then multiply by the rate per $100. The Comptroller puts the ratio at 25 percent for residential and farm property and 40 percent for commercial and industrial property.

Here is the Comptroller's model with a Hamblen-sized home. A house appraised at $210,900 has an assessed value of $52,725. Divide by 100 to get 527.25 and multiply by the tax rate you are billed. A rate of $1.00 would give $527.25, and every extra dollar of rate adds that amount again. The rate is a stand-in here, so use the actual one from the Trustee.

The Assessor's office also handles the countywide reappraisal. After a reappraisal, the Comptroller says a jump in value does not by itself make an assessment wrong, and a judge may disregard it. The owner still has to show the correct number with evidence.

sections.h2: When are Hamblen County property taxes due, and where do I pay?
sections.html:
The county says taxes become due October 1 and delinquent the following March 1. The state schedule adds that payment starts the first Monday of October, which was October 5 this year. It is November 15, 2026 now, so the 2026 bill is open and interest has not started.

Payment choices on the county's tax page:

  • The Trustee's office at the courthouse on West Second North Street
  • The satellite office at 2415 N Davy Crockett Parkway
  • Online at TNPayments.com/Hamblen, which leaves the county website
  • By phone with questions at 423-586-6290

Businesses pay personal property tax on their equipment to the same office on the same schedule. The gross receipts business tax goes to the County Clerk at 423-586-1993.

sections.h2: How can I challenge a Hamblen County assessment?
sections.html:
Call the Assessor first. His office is also the contact point for the Board of Equalization, a five-member panel the county commission appoints. It meets once a year, starting June 1. Some assessors will look at a value informally before the board date, and the state says that is useful but is not an appeal. Ask whether the Hamblen office does.

From the county board, an owner can go to the State Board of Equalization by August 1 or within 45 days of the board's notice, whichever is later. Hearings are held before an administrative judge who must rule within 90 days, and the person appealing carries the burden of proof. The state schedules hearings at 615-401-7883, extension 2.

Evidence that carries weight, per the state:

  • Sales of similar homes with the differences adjusted for
  • An appraisal, with the appraiser prepared to testify
  • A specific value you claim, backed by facts about your property

The undisputed share of the bill has to be paid by the delinquency date, along with any earlier unpaid years.

sections.h2: Does Hamblen County offer property tax relief or a freeze?
sections.html:
Yes, to both. The state relief program reimburses low-income elderly and disabled homeowners and some disabled veterans. For 2026 the income cap is $38,470 based on 2025 income, relief is figured on up to $33,600 of market value, and the veteran program uses up to $175,000. Apply through the county Trustee, with the deadline 35 days after the delinquency date.

Hamblen County is also one of the 28 counties on the Comptroller's tax freeze list. It adopted the freeze in 2007, and the 2026 income limit is $39,260. A homeowner who is 65 by the end of the application year and meets the income cap can lock the tax on a principal residence at the amount owed in the first qualifying year. The owner must apply every year, and the base amount rises if the owner improves the property or sells and buys another home.

sections.h2: What should I do about Hamblen County tax when I sell?
sections.html:
Ownership for the year is fixed on January 1, but the title company prorates the bill between the two sides at the table. Ask the Trustee for a current balance before you list, especially on an inherited house or one with several unpaid years, because delinquent tax gains interest after March 1.

The Hamblen County Clerk and Master's website has a delinquent tax section and a tax search and payment tool, so a seller with old years outstanding can look there or call the office at 423-586-9112. Once the sale is set, the deed goes to the Register of Deeds in the same courthouse, where the state transfer tax is collected.

faqs.q: When are Hamblen County property taxes due?
faqs.a: They become payable in October, and the county lists October 1 as the due date. They turn delinquent on March 1 of the next year. Payment is accepted at the courthouse, the Davy Crockett Parkway satellite office and online.

faqs.q: Who is the Hamblen County property assessor?
faqs.a: Keith Ely holds the office, which is in the courthouse at 511 West Second North Street, Morristown. The phone is 423-586-1852. The office values about 32,000 parcels and prepares the roll for the county and the City of Morristown.

faqs.q: Is there a property tax freeze in Hamblen County?
faqs.a: Yes. The county adopted it in 2007 and the 2026 income limit is $39,260. You must be 65 by the end of the application year, own and live in the home, and reapply annually through the Trustee.

faqs.q: How do I dispute my Hamblen County property value?
faqs.a: Contact the Assessor, then take the dispute to the county Board of Equalization, which meets starting June 1. A later appeal goes to the State Board of Equalization by August 1 or 45 days after the county board's notice.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Hamblen County property tax online?
faqs.a: Use TNPayments.com/Hamblen, the link the county's tax page provides. For questions about a balance, call the Trustee at 423-586-6290.
